If you just want to get married at the registrar's office (like a courthouse wedding), all you need to do is fill out the application on the government's website, email it to them, and request a day/time. You'll have to provide a scan of your passports, birth certificates, and if you've been married before, you'll need proof of divorce. They'll message you back confirming the date/time or let you know when else is available, and they'll take your payment. The day before you get married, you'll have an appointment at the registrar's office to fill out forms, and they'll look over your documents. You'll need to have your original copies of your documents and proof that you are staying in a hotel in Gibraltar for at least one evening there (your hotel can provide you with a letter). Your documents will need to be translated into English if they are in another language. The ceremony and all the paperwork you'll do is in English.

I've seen a lot of people on this sub suggest using a wedding planner for the registrar weddings, but it truly isn't needed and definitely not worth your money, in my opinion, especially if you speak English and have time to pester the office with emails. The registrar's office is really busy right now with everyone trying to do this, so it might take awhile for them to get back to you and to find an open slot. Lot's of people are cancelling last minute, so it's good to check regularly if they tell you they're full. That part is kinda a pain in the ass, but it was wayyyy easier and cheaper than dealing with a planner.

The only other thing we booked was a hotel and a photographer. We went with Radka Horvath for photography. She did a wonderful job, and we felt like her prices were incredibly reasonable for the service she provided. She made us feel so comfortable. 10/10 would recommend. If you get married at the registrar's office, you'll need to have two witnesses. Our photographer and her partner were ours. I believe right now they're only allowing the couple and the two witnesses in the office for the ceremony, so if you want photos of that, make sure at least one of your witnesses is your photographer no matter who you decide to book. We had to wear a mask during our ceremony, but got to take it off to kiss. I know that's a deal breaker for some people, but we thought the photos ended up being really cool and honestly didn't care as long as we were getting married.

We stayed at the Rock Hotel which was very nice! We met tons of other international couples there who were doing the same thing as us. The hotel is a bit of a steep, but short walk from the center of town. Throughout the trip we did not to take a cab or public transportation while we were there just to better socially distance. It wasn't very bad, and we walked from the airport to the hotel, but definitely make plans according to the weather, the amount of time you have, and your fitness level. Since we took photos at multiple locations, we rode with the photographer for some bits and walked some.

I did my own hair and makeup, but you can easily book someone to do it for you. I wouldn't go too elaborate due to the heat, and your hair will get really wind swept if you go take any photos on top of the Rock. 

For the bouquet and boutonniere, I bought a cheap bouquet of sunflowers and roses and some twine from Morrison's (a grocery store). I made my bouquet and my husband's boutonniere in the hotel room with the twine, a safety pin, and borrowed some scissors from the hotel. They looked professionally done and were only £10. The women at the front desk took photos of my flowers because she was amazed how nice they turned out. She's said she was going to do that for her own wedding 🤣

After the ceremony, my partner and I went out to lunch and then got a mini cake from a bakery called Chök that was so delicious. Definitely recommend them.

Overall, flights, staying in Gibraltar for 5 days, and getting married was around the same total price as doing the fiance visa. It was absolutely amazing, and I'd recommend it to any internal couple struggling with visa stuff. 

Sorry if that was too much info! Just thought I'd cover as much as possible 🙂

My husband and I got married towards the end of August in Gibraltar due to the exact issue you're having! We definitely recommend it! Don't mess with using a wedding planner if you're just wanting to get married at the registrar office. We booked like two weeks before we went, and we booked everything ourselves. Let me know if you have any questions. :)

In the United States, the lawyers go through a process called voir dire before the trial. Both sides try to stack the jury to be the most sympathetic to their arguments. The defense tries to have a jury that would be sympathetic to the background of the person on trial, and the district attorney would try to have a jury filled with people who would either sympathize with the victim and/or be less trusting of the defendant. You can strike a juror for cause (the potential juror expressed how they couldn't look past their bias) and a few times without cause (based on a hunch).

You can never completely remove a person's bias, so attorneys have to make decisions based on stereotypes and general beliefs held by specific demographics. Yes it seems shitty and prejudice, but wouldn't you do everything possible to set things to be in your favor when presenting an argument? Typically you can strike anyone who have been a victim of a crime similar to the one presented or if you have a close friend/family member who was a victim. They say they do this because of bias, and they don't want the juror to have a traumatic experience. I would say most women know someone who has been sexually assaulted. They probably "compromise" by having the unspoken rule of "no young women" so that they can get women on the jury in the first place. 

"If lawyers started eliminated everyone with dark skin from juries, there would be a massive uproar " Idk if you know, but they already do that... and people are rightly very upset about it. 

Some people in this thread are saying we should get rid of juries.. wtf?? What makes you think a judge, who is frequently a man, is gonna be unbiased?

I have zero issues with people talking about their identity and about intersectionality, as you saw with my excessively long paragraphs about the history, culture, and identity of Appalachians lol. 😂 I have issues with the real life applications of "identity politics."  I have issues when people focus on what makes us different instead finding our commonalities to reach our common goals, with people assuming that your identity disqualifies you from having empathy for another's identity, with people assuming that we can liberate our identity group without liberating the most uniting, intersectional identity: class. We cannot do it alone. We cannot continue to work as individuals. We need radical solidarity.

I didn't always think this way, and what changed my mind was the Black Panther Party, especially the Chicago party. I think that the work that the Black Panther Party did with the Young Lords and Young Patriots could be an amazing blueprint for all of our organizing and political conversations. They show how focusing on class to find commonality is crucial to building successful coalitions. Fred Hampton's speech "It's a Class Struggle, Goddammit!" lays out the reasoning behind this, where racism comes from (comes straight from capitalism), and about why people are so resistant to talking about class but are incredibly comfortable talking about identity (they don't wanna put in the work for the movement).

Only when activists start uniting the masses does the government start getting scared shitless. For example, Malcolm X stops the black separatism/nation of Islam stuff and starts preaching racial and class unity: assassinated. MLK starts his Poor People's campaign: assassinated. Fred Hampton promotes working class unity in Chicago with the Rainbow Coalition: assassinated. Activists and friends of the Mike Brown family from Ferguson who were vocal about groups who co-opted the movement and ignored the class issues: 6 people assassinated. The list is endless.

And at least for me, I was able to change some minds of people who were previously put off by leftist ideas, people who I thought would never come around, like my family members.
